unit.title: Plan for wiring and installation of electrical/electronic machinery appliances and fixtures

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Before planning the wiring for a new electric water heater, which document gives its supply, protection and clearance needs?
options: The maker's installation instructions
The plumber's invoice for the pipework
The shop's sales receipt for the heater
The warranty card of the old heater

questions.stem: Which information on an appliance's nameplate does the planner use to size its circuit?
options: The colour, model year and serial number
The voltage and the power or current rating
The country where the appliance was made and shipped from
The weight and the size of the packing box

questions.stem: The nameplate on a storage water heater reads 220 V, 4 kW. About what current will it take?
options: 9 A

questions.stem: An appliance rated 1 320 W runs on 110 V. What current does it draw?
options: 6 A

questions.stem: Why is a large air-conditioning unit usually supplied at 220 V rather than 110 V in Jamaica?
options: It draws about half the current, so cable can be smaller
A 220 V supply is always safer to touch than a 110 V supply
A 110 V supply cannot run any kind of electric motor
A 220 V supply runs at a different frequency

questions.stem: A 220 V fixed appliance is fed by two line conductors. Which device protects and isolates it?
options: A single-pole breaker in one line only
A two-pole breaker that opens both lines
A fuse fitted in the neutral conductor
An ordinary light switch fitted on the nearby wall

questions.stem: Why does the maker often ask for a water heater or A/C unit to have its own circuit?
options: So the appliance can be moved more easily later
So a thinner, cheaper cable can be used for it
Its big load could overload a shared circuit
So the breaker for it never needs to be labelled

questions.stem: A pump motor draws a large current for a moment when it starts. What should the planner do about this?
options: Choose the smallest breaker that will fit the board
Leave the motor without any overload protection
Use an ordinary light switch to start the motor
Choose protection that will not trip on normal starting

questions.stem: Why is a local isolator (disconnect switch) planned within sight of an outdoor A/C unit?
options: So it can be isolated and locked off where the work is done
So the unit can be switched on from the garden by the owner
So the breaker in the distribution board is not needed
So the unit uses less power at night when it is cooler

questions.stem: A 30 m run feeds a pump taking 10 A. The Centre's table gives 11 mV/A/m for the chosen cable. What volt drop should the planner expect?
A 220 V circuit has a calculated voltage drop of 5.4 V. The job specification allows 4%. What is the right decision?
options: Not acceptable, because 5.4 V is more than 4 V
Acceptable, because 5.4 V is less than 8.8 V
Not acceptable, because any drop at all is too much
Acceptable, because the limit only applies to lights

questions.stem: A cable run passes through a hot roof space. What should the planner allow for?
options: Use a thinner cable, because heat helps current flow
Nothing, because roof heat has no effect on cable
Paint the cable white so that it reflects the heat
Derate it: heat lowers the current it can safely carry

questions.stem: A pump will be fitted outdoors beside a water tank. What should the planner check on its isolator and connections?
options: A colour that matches the water tank
A rating meant for indoor, dry use only
An IP rating that suits wet, outdoor use
A size small enough to hide behind the tank

questions.stem: A heavy ceiling fan is to be hung from a concrete ceiling. What must the plan include?
options: A fixing point rated for the fan's weight and movement
A plastic box held up only by the supply cable inside it
Fixing the fan to the plaster using glue
Hanging the fan from the light switch drop

questions.stem: The maker's instructions give minimum clearances around an A/C outdoor unit. Why must the planner follow them?
options: So the unit looks neat when seen from the road
For airflow, service access and safe working
So the unit can be painted later by the owner
So the supply cable can be as short as possible

questions.stem: A water heater's switch is needed for a bathroom. Where should the planner place it?
options: Inside the shower, where it is easy to reach
Beside the basin taps, at hand height
On the floor behind the toilet, out of sight
Outside the room, away from water and wet hands

questions.stem: Why must the plan include a protective (earth) conductor to a metal-cased stove?
options: So a fault trips the protection and the case is not left live
So the stove's oven can heat up faster than it normally would
So the stove uses less electricity each month
So the circuit does not need a neutral conductor

questions.stem: Which outlet would the planner most likely protect with a GFCI (RCD)?
options: The main earthing conductor at the board
The low-voltage side of a doorbell transformer
A socket outlet next to the kitchen sink
The supply cable between the meter and the board

questions.stem: A small computer server rack is being planned for an office. Which extra need might the planner add?
options: A dimmer switch on its supply to save power
Surge protection and its own dedicated circuits
A shared circuit with the workshop welder
No earth, so as to stop electrical noise

questions.stem: Three spotlights go along a 9 m display wall, evenly spaced with half a space at each end. How far apart are they?
A motor-driven gate will be controlled from the house and from the gate. Which document should the planner study for the control wiring?
options: The house's plumbing layout drawing
A drawing for a different make of gate
The receipt from the shop for the motor
The maker's wiring diagram for the controller

questions.stem: Why does the planner visit the site before finishing the plan for a new stove circuit?
options: To check the route, board space and existing wiring
To meet the neighbours and tell them all about the job
To measure the inside of the new stove's oven
To help the client choose a colour for the hood

questions.stem: The survey finds the distribution board has no spare ways for the new A/C circuit. What is the best plan?
options: Connect the A/C into an existing lighting breaker
Plan a larger or extra board, agreed with the client
Put two cables under one breaker terminal
Run the A/C from an extension cord to an outlet

questions.stem: Why should the planner check the total load on the supply before adding a large appliance?
options: The power company charges less for large loads
Large appliances lower the total load on a house
The main supply and main breaker may not carry the extra
The meter will only work with small appliances

questions.stem: Which group of items belongs on the materials list for installing a 220 V split A/C unit?
options: A single-pole 6 A breaker and lighting cable
A dimmer switch and some flexible lamp cord
A plug-in adapter and a long extension lead
A two-pole breaker, isolator, cable and conduit

questions.stem: What does a method statement for installing a stove circuit set out?
options: The steps of the work in order, with the safety controls
Only the list of materials and their prices
The client's schedule of payments for each stage of the job
The test results recorded after the job is done

questions.stem: When planning a new circuit in an occupied home, which hazard should the risk assessment include?
options: The client's choice of curtains and paint
The colour of the cable sheath used
Drilling into hidden cables or water pipes
The size of the van parked outside

questions.stem: The plan includes work inside the existing distribution board. Which step must the plan include before any connection is made?
options: Work quickly so that the power is off for less time
Isolate, lock off, tag, and prove dead with a checked tester
Switch the breaker off and start work straight away
Ask the client not to touch any switches at all while you work

questions.stem: Which order is best for installing a new fixed-appliance circuit?
options: Connect at the board, run the cable, then fix the appliance
Fix the appliance, run the cable, terminate and test, then connect at the board
Test the new circuit first, then run the cable, connect the board, and fix the appliance
Run the cable, energise it, then connect the appliance to it

questions.stem: Who should the planner talk to about the position of the supply point for an A/C indoor unit?
options: The power company's meter reader only
The firm that supplied the cable
The painter who will finish the walls
The A/C installer and the client

questions.stem: The test plan for a water heater circuit lists the checks done before the supply is switched on. Which set is right?
options: Continuity, insulation resistance and polarity, done dead
Only a check that the appliance switches on and runs normally
A live test by touching the terminals with a tester
A check of the paint finish around the appliance

questions.stem: Why should the maker's manual be left with the appliance after installation?
options: So the warranty can never run out
So users and servicers follow its advice
So the electrician can sell it on later
So it can be moved without being isolated

questions.stem: Which route should the planner choose for a stove circuit cable?
options: The longest route, so the cable can be moved later
Loose across the floor and under the kitchen rug
The shortest safe route, away from heat and damage
Through the same sleeve as the gas supply pipe

questions.stem: A recessed light fitting is to go into a ceiling that has roof insulation. What should the plan check?
options: That the fitting is the cheapest one available
That insulation is packed tightly round the lamp
That the lamp is the highest wattage made
That it is rated for insulation, or keep it clear

questions.stem: Why is a fire alarm or security panel supply usually planned on its own labelled circuit?
options: So it is not switched off by mistake with others
So it can share a circuit with the kitchen
So it can run without any protective device
So the standby battery inside it is never needed

questions.stem: Why does the planner estimate the labour hours for each task in the installation plan?
options: To decide the colour of the conduit
To set the programme and the cost
To choose which appliance to buy
To work out the breaker's rating

questions.stem: The client wants a 220 V stove, but the house has only a 110 V supply. What should the planner do?
options: Connect the stove to 110 V and see if it works
Join two 110 V outlets together to make 220 V
Explain a 220 V supply is needed and plan it
Fit a smaller fuse inside the stove's casing

questions.stem: Which fixing is best for mounting a heavy isolator on a concrete block wall?
options: Nails driven into the mortar joints
Strong double-sided adhesive tape
Cable ties looped round a nearby pipe
Wall plugs and screws sized for the load

questions.stem: When planning the fitting of an electronic control board for a gate motor, why include anti-static precautions?
options: Static from hands can damage electronic parts
Static makes the control board run more slowly
Static makes the board heavier to fix in place
Static only matters for boards used outdoors

questions.stem: A kitchen circuit at 110 V will feed a 1 100 W microwave and a 1 650 W kettle at the same time. What is the total current?
Two kitchen appliances used together draw 25 A at 110 V. The outlet circuit is protected at 20 A. What is the best plan?
options: Fit a 32 A breaker on the existing cable
Put the two appliances on separate circuits
Plug both into a double adapter on one outlet
Tell the client the breaker will just reset itself

questions.stem: Why should the plan include updating the circuit chart in the board?
options: So the client knows what the work cost
So the inspector does not need to test
So the new circuit can be found and isolated
So the board door can be left open

questions.stem: Which part of the plan protects the client's home while the work is done?
options: Leaving the cable offcuts for the client to clear
Moving the furniture without asking the client
Drilling first and looking for pipes afterwards
Dust sheets, floor covers and a daily clean-up

questions.stem: An outdoor pump draws 9 A running. Which isolator is suitable?
options: A weatherproof isolator rated above 9 A
An indoor light switch rated at 5 A
A weatherproof isolator rated at 5 A
A plug and outlet left lying on the ground

questions.stem: Before any fixing begins on site, whose approval should the installation plan carry?
options: Only the newest trainee on the team
The supervisor and, where needed, the client
The shop where the appliance was bought
Nobody, because plans need no approval

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A cooker's nameplate says 4.4 kW, 220 V. Work out its full-load current in amps.
What is the plate on an appliance that gives its voltage, power and current called?
What is the switch fitted near an appliance, so it can be switched off and locked off there, called?
What word means lowering a cable's current rating because of heat, grouping or insulation around it?
What is the written step-by-step plan of how a task will be done safely called?
What device protects electronic equipment from voltage spikes, for example from lightning? (words or letters)
How many line conductors feed a 220 V fixed appliance in a typical Jamaican home?
What is the maker's drawing that shows how an appliance's terminals and controls are connected called?
Six LED lights of 18 W each are on one circuit. What is the total load, in watts?
What is the short burst of extra current a motor draws at the moment it starts called?
How many cycles each second does Jamaica's mains supply make (its frequency, in Hz)?
Which dead test, done with a low-resistance ohmmeter, confirms that the earth conductor is unbroken from the board to the appliance?
What is the list of all the circuits in a board, with their breaker sizes and what they feed, called?
Give the short name of the device that trips when current leaks to earth, to protect people from shock.
A pump motor is rated 0.75 kW. How many watts is that?

essays.stem: You are asked to plan the installation of a 220 V electric water heater in a Kingston home. Describe the information you would collect and the decisions you would make before work starts.
essays.modelAnswer: I would read the maker's installation instructions and the nameplate to find the voltage, power and current, the protection it needs, and the clearances and fixing it requires. I would survey the house: the supply and the main breaker, spare ways in the board, the condition of the existing wiring and earthing, and the cable route to the heater. From the current I would choose a two-pole breaker of the right rating and size the cable from the Centre's tables, allowing for the route and voltage drop. I would plan a local isolator near the heater but away from water, a protective conductor to the heater, and GFCI (RCD) protection if the code the Centre uses asks for it. I would list the materials and tools, write a method statement and risk assessment that include safe isolation, plan the dead tests, agree the timing with the client and the plumber, and get the plan approved.
markingPoints: Reads maker's instructions and nameplate data
Surveys the supply, board, wiring, earthing and route
Chooses a two-pole breaker and sizes the cable from tables
Plans isolator position, earthing and GFCI as required
Materials, method statement with safe isolation, test plan, coordination and approval

essays.stem: Explain how you would work out the circuit protection and cable size for a new fixed appliance, using its nameplate and the cable tables the Centre provides.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would find the design current from the nameplate, either the current given or the power divided by the voltage, for example 3 300 W at 220 V gives 15 A. Next I would choose a protective device rated at or just above that current, of a type that suits the load, for example one that will not trip on a motor's starting current. Then I would choose a cable whose current rating, after correction for the conditions, is at least the breaker rating. The correction factors cover things like a hot roof space, cables grouped together or cable run in insulation. Then I would check voltage drop: the table's millivolts per amp per metre, times the current, times the length, divided by 1000, must be within the limit the specification gives. If it is too high I would choose a larger cable. Finally I would check that the cable and breaker suit the maker's instructions.
markingPoints: Finds design current from the nameplate (I = P ÷ V)
Chooses a breaker rated at or above the design current, of a suitable type
Chooses a cable rated at least the breaker after correction factors
Names correction factors such as heat, grouping and insulation
Checks voltage drop with the mV/A/m method and the limit; checks against the maker's instructions

essays.stem: Describe what you would check during a site survey before planning the installation of a split A/C unit.
essays.modelAnswer: I would check the supply: whether there is 220 V available, the size of the main breaker and the existing load, so the extra load can be carried. I would look at the distribution board for a spare way and its condition, and check the earthing. I would agree with the client and the A/C installer where the indoor and outdoor units will go, and check the wall is strong enough for the fixings. I would look at the route for the cable from the board to the outdoor isolator and to the indoor unit, measuring the length and noting walls, ceilings and hot or wet areas. I would check that the outdoor position has the clearances the maker asks for and that the isolator can be placed within sight of the unit. I would note hazards such as work at height, and any existing faults to report. I would record all of this with measurements and photos.
markingPoints: Checks supply voltage, main breaker and existing load
Checks the board for a spare way, its condition and earthing
Agrees unit positions with the client and installer; checks fixings
Plans and measures the cable route and isolator position; maker's clearances
Notes hazards and existing faults; records with measurements and photos

essays.stem: Explain why a means of isolation is planned close to fixed machinery and appliances, and describe how it would be used for safe isolation.
essays.modelAnswer: A local isolator lets the person servicing the machine switch it off at the place where they work, without going back to the board, which may be far away or locked. It must be within sight or able to be locked off, so nobody can switch it back on while someone is working. It also lets the machine be switched off quickly in an emergency. For safe isolation, the worker first identifies the correct isolator, switches it off, and fits their own padlock and a tag with their name, the date and the reason. They check their voltage indicator on a proving unit, then test between all the conductors at the machine to prove it is dead, and check the indicator again on the proving unit. Only then is the work started. Work is never done live. When the work is done and tested, the lock is removed and the supply restored by the authorised person.
markingPoints: Lets the worker isolate at the point of work
Within sight or lockable, so nobody can switch it on
Allows quick emergency switching off
Safe isolation steps: off, lock, tag, prove dead with tester checked before and after
No live work; lock removed and supply restored only after work and tests

essays.stem: Compare the planning needs for installing a 110 V ceiling fan and a 220 V stove. Say what is different and why.
essays.modelAnswer: A ceiling fan uses a small current, so it can usually be fed from a lighting circuit through its own switch or speed control, with a single-pole breaker on the 110 V circuit. The main planning points for the fan are the fixing, which must carry its weight and the movement as it turns, the height of the blades above the floor, and the control position. A stove uses a large current at 220 V, so it needs its own circuit fed from two line conductors with a two-pole breaker, a much larger cable sized from the tables, a stove isolator within reach but not over the hot plates, and a good protective conductor to its metal case. The stove needs a check that the main supply can carry the extra load. Both need the maker's instructions, safe isolation, dead testing and an updated circuit chart.
markingPoints: Fan: small load, can use the lighting circuit with a single-pole breaker
Fan: fixing for weight and movement, blade height, control position
Stove: own 220 V circuit, two-pole breaker, larger cable
Stove: isolator position, earth to metal case, check main supply capacity
Both: maker's instructions, safe isolation, testing and circuit chart

essays.stem: Explain how the place where an appliance is installed (outdoors, in a bathroom, or in a hot roof space) affects the choice of equipment and cable.
essays.modelAnswer: Outdoors, equipment is exposed to rain, dust and strong sun, so the isolator, enclosures and glands must have an IP rating that suits wet outdoor use, and cables must resist sunlight or be in conduit. Fixings should not rust. In a bathroom, water and wet skin raise the risk of shock, so switches and controls are placed outside the room or out of reach of the bath or shower, as the code the Centre uses allows, and GFCI (RCD) protection is usually needed. Equipment near water must be rated for it. In a hot roof space, the high temperature lowers the current a cable can carry, so the cable must be derated and may need to be larger, and equipment must be rated for the heat. In all places the maker's instructions set the limits, and the planner records the choices in the plan.
markingPoints: Outdoors: suitable IP rating, sun-resistant cable or conduit, rust-proof fixings
Bathroom: controls outside or out of reach, GFCI protection, equipment rated for water
Hot roof: derate the cable, larger size if needed, equipment rated for heat
Follows the maker's instructions and the code the Centre uses

essays.stem: Describe the parts of a method statement and risk assessment for installing a pump motor and its controls.
essays.modelAnswer: The method statement gives the job details, the drawings and the maker's instructions used. It lists the people, their roles and their competence, and the tools, test instruments and materials. It sets out the steps in order: survey and marking out, fixing the pump base and control panel, running the cable and conduit, fitting the local isolator, terminating at the pump and panel, inspection and dead testing, and connection at the board last. It states that safe isolation is used for any work at the board, with lock, tag and proving dead with a tester checked before and after, and that no live work is done. The risk assessment lists the hazards, such as electric shock, water near the pump, manual handling of the motor, drilling and dust, and hot weather. For each it gives who could be harmed, the controls, such as PPE and safe lifting, and the person responsible. Both are signed and briefed to the team.
markingPoints: Method statement: job details, documents, people, tools and materials
Steps in order with connection at the board last
Safe isolation stated; no live work
Risk assessment: hazards such as shock, water, lifting, drilling, heat, with controls
Signed and briefed to the team

essays.stem: Explain how you would plan the order of work and coordinate with other trades when fitting a set of kitchen appliances in a new house.
essays.modelAnswer: I would get the kitchen layout from the client or kitchen fitter, with the position of the stove, fridge, microwave, kettle points, extractor hood and any water heater. From it I would plan the circuits and the positions of outlets and isolators. First fix conduit and boxes go in before the walls are plastered, and positions are agreed with the kitchen fitter so they are not hidden behind cabinets. I would agree with the plumber where the pipes run, so cables stay clear of water. After plastering, the cables are pulled in. Second fix happens after the cabinets and worktops are fitted and the painter has done the first coat. The appliances are connected last, then the circuits are inspected and tested dead, and the instructor or authorised person energises them. I would put these stages on the builder's programme and confirm them at site meetings.
markingPoints: Gets the kitchen layout and plans circuits and positions
First fix before plaster, positions agreed with the kitchen fitter
Routes agreed with the plumber, away from water
Second fix after cabinets and painting; appliances connected last; tested dead before energising
Stages put on the programme and confirmed at site meetings

essays.stem: Describe the tests you would plan for a new appliance circuit, why each is done dead, and who energises it.
essays.modelAnswer: I would plan a visual inspection first, to check the cable, terminations, isolator, earth connection and labels. Then the dead tests: continuity of the protective conductor from the board to the appliance's metal case, to show a fault current has a path; continuity of the line and neutral conductors; insulation resistance between conductors and to earth, to show the insulation is sound and there is no short; and polarity, to show the breaker and switches are in the line conductor. These are done dead, after safe isolation, because the instruments and the person must not be exposed to the supply, and an insulation tester puts a high test voltage on the circuit. Results are recorded and compared with the limits. Only when every test has passed does the instructor, or the authorised person on a real job, energise the circuit and carry out any live checks such as the GFCI trip test.
markingPoints: Visual inspection first
Protective conductor continuity and conductor continuity
Insulation resistance and polarity, with reasons
Done dead after safe isolation, and why
Results recorded; only the instructor or authorised person energises and does live checks

essays.stem: Explain what information and documents should be handed to the client after an appliance is installed, and why.
essays.modelAnswer: The client should receive the maker's manual, so they can use, clean and look after the appliance correctly and safely. They should receive the warranty card and the date of installation, so they can claim if it fails. They should get the test results for the new circuit, which show it was tested and is safe, and which the next electrician can compare with. The circuit chart in the board must be updated, so the right breaker can be found to isolate the appliance. I would show the client where the local isolator and the breaker are, how to switch the appliance off in an emergency, and how to test a GFCI outlet if one is fitted. I would also give our contact details and explain how often the appliance should be serviced. I would ask the client to sign that they have received everything.
markingPoints: Maker's manual for safe use and care
Warranty and installation date
Test results for the circuit
Updated circuit chart; shows isolator, breaker and GFCI test
Contact details, servicing advice and signed receipt

practical1.title: Plan the wiring for a set of appliances and fixtures in a small house
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a floor plan of a small house with its 110/220 V supply, an existing board with three spare ways, the nameplate data for the appliances (a 3 300 W 220 V water heater, a 220 V split A/C unit drawing 9 A, a 220 V stove, two ceiling fans, an outdoor 110 V pump drawing 9 A, and the kitchen outlets), cable tables with mV/A/m values and correction factors, and a voltage-drop limit for this job. As a planning team, produce an installation plan: (1) a load schedule with the current for each item and the total; (2) the circuits, with protection type and rating, and whether each needs a two-pole breaker or GFCI (RCD) protection; (3) cable sizes with correction factors and a voltage-drop check for the longest runs; (4) a marked-up floor plan showing routes, isolators, outlets and fixing points; (5) a materials and tools list; (6) a method statement and risk assessment that include safe isolation; (7) a test plan; and (8) a short note on the board's spare ways and any upgrade needed. Each member leads two items and checks another member's work. The group presents the plan to the assessor. Photograph each stage.
materials: Floor plan, supply details and appliance nameplate data (from the assessor)
Cable tables with mV/A/m values, correction factors and the voltage-drop limit
Blank load schedule, circuit schedule, materials list, method statement, risk assessment and test plan forms
Scale rules, coloured pens and calculators
Makers' installation leaflets for the appliances, or copies from the assessor
photos: The load schedule with currents worked out
The circuit schedule with protection choices
The cable size and voltage-drop working
The method statement and risk assessment
checklist: Worked out currents correctly from the nameplate data
Chose suitable protection, including two-pole breakers for 220 V and GFCI where needed
Sized cables using the tables, correction factors and a correct voltage-drop check
Placed isolators and outlets sensibly and to the makers' instructions
Included safe isolation (off, lock, tag, prove dead with a tester checked before and after) in the method statement
Checked another member's work and corrected errors
Explained their part clearly and answered questions
safety: This is a planning task: no supply is used
Plan every task so that no work is done live
Keep the room tidy, with bags and cables off the floor
Follow the Centre's rules for the classroom

practical2.title: Survey, mark out and prepare a training bay for a fixed appliance installation
practical2.brief: On one of the Centre's training bays (never connected to a supply), the group plans and prepares the installation of a 220 V fixed appliance, such as a split A/C indoor unit or a water heater, using a mock-up or the real appliance and its maker's instructions. As a team: (1) survey the bay and the training board, and record what you find; (2) read the maker's instructions and nameplate and note the supply, protection, clearances and fixing needs; (3) write a short method statement and risk assessment; (4) carry out and record safe isolation of the training board (switch off, lock off, tag, prove dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after); (5) mark out the positions of the isolator, the appliance supply point and the cable route; (6) fix the boxes, isolator enclosure and conduit or trunking to the plan, but make no connection at the board; and (7) complete a pre-installation checklist ready for the wiring stage. Each member leads one step and every member does some of the fixing. Only the instructor may energise anything. Photograph each stage.
materials: Training bay and training board (not connected to any supply)
Mock-up or real 220 V appliance with its maker's instructions and nameplate
Isolator enclosure, boxes, conduit or trunking, saddles and fixings
Spirit level, tape measure, chalk line or laser level, pencil
Drill, bits, hand tools and insulated screwdrivers
Lock-off kit, danger tags, voltage indicator and proving unit
Survey sheet, method statement and risk assessment forms, pre-installation checklist
photos: The survey sheet and the maker's data noted
The training board locked off and tagged, and the tester being checked
The marked-out positions and cable route on the bay
The boxes, isolator and conduit or trunking fixed in place
A level check on the isolator and supply point
checklist: Recorded the survey and the maker's requirements accurately
Carried out safe isolation correctly before any work
Marked out positions level, to the plan and within the maker's clearances
Fixed boxes, isolator and conduit or trunking firmly and neatly
Used tools safely and wore the right PPE
Completed their part of the method statement, risk assessment or checklist
Left the bay clean and tidy at the end
safety: The training bay is never connected to a supply; only the instructor energises anything
Prove dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after, with each member's own lock and tag
Wear safety glasses when drilling and cutting; check for hidden cables before drilling
Use steps safely, with one person holding them for work above head height
Lift the appliance or mock-up with two people, keeping the back straight
